full_judgment:
2. Short facts necessary for disposal of this petition for leave to appeal are that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No.184 of 1999 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Pabna for declaration of title to the inn land stating, inter-alia, that the suit land was purchased by plaintiff No.1 and one Sokiruddin by kabala dated 07.12.1955 from its owner and in the S.A. Khatian their names were recorded to the extent of 22 decimals of land instead of 26 decimals. Sokiruddin transferred 13 decimals of land to plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 by sale dated 05.12.1948. Plaintiff' Nos. 2 and 3 sold .0375 acre of land to plaintiff No. 4 by a kabala dated 23.11.1996. The plaintiffs have been possessing 26 decimals of from the middle of the suit plot by excluding 34 decimals of land from the northern side. In R.S. operation, the land was recorded in their names in R.S. plot No.2274 but not in the northern side of the previous plot. The plaintiffs by amending the plaint stated that the ex-landlord of the suit land was Tarash Estate which after evicting its tenants gave 32 decimals of land by patton which was demarcated by the surveyor of Tarash Acquired Estate. Abdul Mannan filed Other Class Suit No. 25 of 1954 (no name of the Court is available from the record) for recovery of khas possession in which he got decree. 

 3. The defendant Government contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit land was the excess khas land of the ex-landlord as bazaar and the some vested in the Government after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into being. The suit land is within the periphery of Dhulauri hat. The plaintiffs filed the suit by creating some forged documents and as such, the same was liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Defendant Nos.3 and 4 also filed written statement contending, inter-alia, that 24 decimals of land of the suit jute belonged to Abdullah who transferred the same to Abdul Mannan. Abdullah transferred 12 decimals of land being the guardian of his minor son Abdul Mannan to defendant Nos. 3 and 4 by a deed dated 17.12.1957. Abdullah transferred 22 decimals of land to the defendants by another deed dated 15.11.1967 and they are possessing the suit land. 

 7. We have gone through the judgments of the Courts below as well as the High Court Division. From the judgment passed by the trial Court, it appears that the trial Court after considering the evidence on record both oral and documentary came to the specific finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The trial Court further found that in fact the suit land is within the periphery of Dhulauri hat, so the plaintiffs could not have any claim therein. With the above findings the trial Court dismissed the suit. The appellate Court which is the last Court of fact also dismissed the appeal with specific finding to the effect "There is no document to show that the C.S. recorded tenants made transfer of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff-appellant or their predecessors in interest in any way." The appellate Court further found that although by amending the plaint the plaintiffs stated that they purchased the suit land subsequently from Abdul Mannan vide exit.-3(ga) who got decree in Other Class Suit No.25 of 1954 but there is not a single scrap of paper to show that Abdul Mannan got the suit land from the C.S. recorded tenants. The appellate Court further observed that the trial Court rightly found that there was no basis of preparation of S.A. record in the name of plaintiff No.1 and Sokiruddin. The appellate Court further found that though the defendant' government did not produce any document to show that the suit land is within Dhulauri hat periphery "but in spite of that fact this Court is unable to opine that the plaintiff-appellants and their predecessor acquired any valid title to the suit land and there was a legal footing in support of the preparation of the S.A. or R.S. record". From the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the learned Judge observed that the trial Court as well as the appellate Court considered all aspects thoroughly and concurrently found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case. The High Court Division further observed that the decisions of both the Courts below were based "on facts, circumstances and evidence on record. The High Court Division further observed that the learned Advocate for the petitioners failed to make out a case of misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence in arriving at the said findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below and, accordingly discharged the Rule Appellate Division Cases (Criminal)
